conclusion: The add-to-cart operation succeeded server-side, but the Buy Now flow did not observe its own success and did not navigate to checkout.
The watchdog displayed a false timeout while the item had already been added. A user retry can therefore add a duplicate quantity.
Acceptance criteria 2 and 3 fail on the ordinary PDP path, so sticky/double-click/additional branches cannot close the issue.
source_observation: The production handler waits for added_to_cart or custom tt4m:added_to_cart, then uses a 10-second watchdog reset.
The observed successful server-side add did not produce the success transition consumed by the handler.

passes: Policy now inventories Checkout, Contact/B2B, Comment, Account and VAT form data.
Policy now lists Sourcebuster cookie names and session/30-minute retention, local/session storage groups, Google Maps, Google Fonts, Cloudflare and Gravatar.
Contact/comment notices and the unchecked comment persistence checkbox remain documented from prior rounds.
blockers: The policy describes Sourcebuster as traffic/source optimization and calls it analytics-like storage, but does not classify it as essential or optional with a concrete necessity rationale.
No first-party accept/reject/change-choice control is visible; all seven sbjs cookies are written before any user choice.
The policy tells users to use browser deletion/blocking instead of providing the optional-tracking control required by the existing acceptance criteria.
Therefore acceptance criteria 1 and 5 remain unproved/failed despite the improved inventory.
